constraints: Training and existing sleep blocks are protected, so none are moved or deleted.
The Tuesday late-night Serenata conflicts with the protected sleep window before 07:00 training, so it must be declined.
Regular lectures can be removed because the request states they are suspended for Academic Week.
The Wednesday picnic fits between physio and afternoon training but still needs RSVP confirmation.
The Friday dinner ends before the 22:30 sleep block, but attendance still needs RSVP confirmation.
Venue availability, exact travel time and any food logistics are not confirmed.
priorities: The freed lecture hours are used for the requested 4 hours of exam study.
Daytime and early-evening social events are preferred over late-night events.
The plan preserves all high-priority training, sleep and health commitments.

alternatives_considered.option: Use Wednesday 11:00–12:00 plus Thursday morning for study
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Rejected because the removed lecture slots already provide the full 4 hours with less fragmentation.

alternatives_considered.option: Attend part of the Tuesday Serenata only
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Rejected because even partial attendance during 23:30–03:00 violates the protected sleep block.

alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Rejected because it does not conflict with protected commitments and ends before sleep.

rationale.summary: Attend the Wednesday picnic and Friday dinner, decline the Tuesday late-night Serenata, remove the suspended lectures, and use the freed Monday and Tuesday morning lecture slots for 4 hours of exam study while adding Friday night sleep protection.

events.title: Student Association Outdoor Picnic & Lunch on campus

result_calendar.metadata_note: Added-event metadata is copied from validated Proposal fields without inference.

weaknesses: The rationale protects fixed sleep and training well, but it leans too heavily on technical non-conflict. It rejects skipping the Friday dinner mainly because it does not conflict with protected commitments, without weighing the cumulative load of five consecutive days with morning training from 07:00–09:00 and afternoon training from 16:30–18:30.

The Monday and Tuesday exam study blocks from 10:00–12:00 come one hour after 07:00–09:00 training and before lunch at 12:30. That may be workable, but the rationale does not discuss whether these are likely to be effective study periods after physical training rather than merely available former lecture slots.

The Wednesday picnic from 12:30–15:00 sits between sports physiotherapy at 10:00–11:00 and afternoon training at 16:30–18:30. This is not an objective conflict, but it leaves limited visible recovery or preparation margin on a day already containing recovery, social time and training.

The Friday dinner from 19:30–21:30 follows afternoon tactical training ending at 18:30 and precedes sleep at 22:30. The one-hour gaps on both sides may be enough, especially if nearby, but travel, showering, decompression and bedtime preparation are not substantiated.

The proposal deletes Monday and Tuesday lectures based on the stated rationale that lectures are suspended for Academic Week. That may be correct, but from the visible evidence here it remains an unverified condition rather than something independently demonstrated by the calendar.

The alternatives considered are relevant, especially declining the late-night Serenata, but the social-load alternative is dismissed too narrowly on the basis of no protected-event conflict rather than overall sustainability.
critic_evaluation.feedback: The plan is mostly coherent and has several human-centered strengths: it preserves fixed sleep, training and physio; avoids the late-night event before early training; and uses the removed lecture slots for exam study rather than pushing study into evenings. The main concern is not a technical clash but cumulative manageability. Across the visible week, the user has early sleep-to-training transitions every weekday, two daily training sessions on most days, exam study added immediately after morning training on Monday and Tuesday, a long social lunch on Wednesday between physio and afternoon training, and an evening social event on Friday after the final afternoon training session. That may still be manageable for this person, but the rationale does not show enough consideration of recovery, transitions, or the effectiveness of study after training. A stronger plan would either substantiate why these additions are realistic in the user’s fuller context or reconsider whether both social events should remain given the visible training density. I cannot verify whether the original request is fully satisfied, because the original request and any hidden preferences are not available.

plausibility_review.reason: A concrete human-quality risk remains: the proposal adds low-importance social events and immediate post-training study blocks into a week already showing daily early training and repeated afternoon training, while the rationale mostly treats free slots and absence of protected-event conflicts as sufficient. This could affect recovery, study quality and bedtime practicality, especially on Friday where training ends at 18:30, dinner runs 19:30–21:30, and sleep starts at 22:30. The issue is not objectively impossible, and the same operations may be defensible, but the current rationale does not sufficiently justify the sustainability of the full routine.
plausibility_review.suggested_improvement: Reconsider the cumulative load using the fuller context: explain whether the post-training study periods and the Wednesday and Friday social events are realistically compatible with recovery, travel, food, hygiene and bedtime preparation, or reduce the added social load if that context is not supportive.

events.title: Student Association Outdoor Picnic & Lunch on campus

result_calendar.metadata_note: Added-event metadata is copied from validated Proposal fields without inference.

weaknesses: The revised proposal materially improves the prior study-load concern by reducing Monday and Tuesday study from 10:00–12:00 to 10:00–11:30 and adding a shorter Thursday 10:00–11:00 block, but all three exam blocks still occur one hour after 07:00–09:00 training. That is plausible, but the calendar does not show whether post-training recovery, showering, food, or energy levels make these effective study periods rather than merely available time.

The Friday evening remains the tightest part of the plan: afternoon tactical training ends at 18:30, the dinner runs 19:30–21:30, and sleep starts at 22:30. The rationale now correctly treats RSVP, travel, recovery, hygiene and bedtime preparation as conditions, but the resulting calendar still depends heavily on those narrow margins working in practice.

The Wednesday picnic from 12:30–15:00 is more plausible than the Friday dinner because it has visible gaps after 10:00–11:00 physiotherapy and before 16:30–18:30 training, but it still adds a 2.5-hour social event into a day already containing recovery care and afternoon training. This is not a conflict, only a moderate sustainability consideration.

The proposal deletes Monday and Tuesday class events based on an Academic Week suspension. The rationale is transparent that this is user-stated and not independently verified, so the deletion is proportionate only if that condition is true.

The social events are importance 2 while training, sleep, meals and exams are higher importance. The rationale explains why the late-night event is declined and why these events are conditional, but it could still more directly justify why keeping both social events is worthwhile in a visibly dense training week.
critic_evaluation.feedback: The revised plan is substantially more human-centered than the prior version. It responds to the earlier concern by distributing the 4 hours of exam study across three shorter morning blocks instead of two longer post-training blocks, and it explicitly recognizes practical margins around RSVP, food, travel, hygiene, recovery and bedtime. The visible week remains demanding, but much of that load comes from preserved high-priority training and sleep rather than from the proposal itself. The added study and social events appear plausible if the stated conditions are true, especially because the proposal avoids evening study and rejects the late-night Serenata before early training. I would not require another revision on the current evidence, but the Proposer should keep the social events conditional in its fuller context and be prepared to drop or shorten them if the unverified logistics do not support recovery and bedtime. I cannot verify original request satisfaction because the original request and hidden preferences are not available.

plausibility_review.reason: The main prior concern received a grounded answer: the study load was reduced per day and distributed, the late-night social option was rejected to protect sleep, and the rationale now explicitly flags the practical conditions needed for the Wednesday and Friday social events. The remaining risks are real but conditional rather than showing a concrete unsupported organization that clearly needs another revision. The Friday dinner is still tight after 16:30–18:30 training and before 22:30 sleep, but the proposal acknowledges this dependency rather than treating a free slot as automatically sufficient.
plausibility_review.suggested_improvement: Use the fuller context to verify the stated conditions before relying on the social additions, especially Friday travel, recovery, hygiene and bedtime preparation. If those conditions are weak, reconsider the social load rather than adding more commitments around the fixed training and sleep routine.
